newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-U.S. REACH DUNHILL CUP FINAL AFTER DISPUTE IN THIRD MATCH.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-U.S. REACH DUNHILL CUP FINAL AFTER DISPUTE IN THIRD MATCH.

text.p: The top-seeded United States beat Sweden 2-1 in the semifinals of the Dunhill Cup on Sunday despite a fractious final match between Phil Mickelson and Jarmo Sandelin.
The two players had a verbal altercation on the 12th hole before Sweden's Sandelin, who birdied five of the first 12 holes, won 68-71.
Sandelin, 29, said later that Mickelson had criticised the way the Swede had been playing on the U.S. tour this year and had said he should show more respect.
Mickelson said he had spoken to Sandelin about what he felt was the Swede's over-reaction whenever he made a putt.
"I felt our match could have been conducted with a little more sportsmanship than it was. I was disappointed with the way things went out there," he said.
"I did speak to him about it at the 12th but everything is fine now," the American added.

Victories from Mark O'Meara and Steve Stricker, fourth and fifth on the U.S. money list this year, sent the U.S. team into the final later on Sunday, against New Zealand, who beat South Africa 2-1 in the other semifinal.
New Zealand advanced when Grant Waite beat Wayne Westner on the third hole of a playoff.
O'Meara, who shot a 63 on Thursday, beat Peter Hedblom 68-74 in the first of the three encounters .
Stricker remained unbeaten for the week by defeating Patrick Sjoland 70-73 in the middle match to seal the decision.
O'Meara birdied three of the first six holes and was always in control against Hedblom while Stricker had a front nine of 32 against Sjoland.
Mickelson trailed Sandelin by just one shot at the turn but three successive bogeys from the 11th left him too far behind.

"I just feel the Dunhill Cup, the Ryder Cup and the President's Cup are wonderful events that promote sportsmanship and camaderie internationally," Mickelson said later. "I think it's important to keep those events in high esteem."
The Americans could become the first nation to win this title three times if they beat New Zealand in the final.
In the other semifinal, world number four Ernie Els overcame two early bogeys by firing birdies at seven holes out of eight from the fifth, including five in a row.
He double-bogeyed the 17th but his 69 was three shots better than Frank Nobilo.
Greg Turner defeated Retief Goosen 71-72 and it all came down to the playoff between Waite and Westner.
Both players missed the green at the third playoff hole and Westner from an awkward position left his third shot 25 feet from the pin.
Waite rolled up a superb wedge shot to a foot and when Westner's putt stayed just right of the hole, the tie was over.
